paragraphs.text: Thou, O my Church, that now liest in pulvere vastitatis, as a forlorn captive, rouse up thyself, change both thy countenance and condition; Tanquam libera ac laeta ad novum nuncium; up, and look up, I have joyful tidings for thee.
paragraphs.anchor: Arise.

paragraphs.text: Christ, who is αυτοφως - light essential. {Joh 12:46}
paragraphs.anchor: For thy light is come.

paragraphs.text: The glorious gospel of grace. {2Co 3:7; 2Co 4:4}
paragraphs.anchor: And, the glory of the Lord is risen upon thee.

paragraphs.text: As once it did Egypt, {Exo 10:21} when there was light in the land of Goshen. So is there in the Church, when all the world besides lieth buried in a fog of ignorance and a bog of wickedness. Rhodes is always located in the sun. {a} The separation of the saints in light is a wonderful separation. {Exo 33:16}
paragraphs.anchor: For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth.

paragraphs.text: The Lord Christ, who is "the true light," {Joh 1:9} "the light of the world," {Joh 8:12} "the Sun of righteousness." {Mal 4:2} {See Trapp on "Mal 4:2"}
paragraphs.anchor: But the Lord shall arise upon thee.

paragraphs.text: {a} Semper in sole sita est Rhodos.

The apostles, those shining luminaries, were Christ’s Dαδουχοι, holding forth the light of life to all people, as Simeon said. {Luk 2:34-35} And we may well say, as our Saviour did, {Luk 4:21} This day is this Scripture fulfilled in our ears, and made good to our hearts, praised be his holy name throughout all eternity.
paragraphs.anchor: And the Gentiles shall come to thy light.

paragraphs.text: As did our King Lucius, who is reckoned to be the first Christian king; our Constantine, the first Christian emperor; our Edward VI, the first reforming prince, and many others. Facit hoc contra Anabaptistas, qui exclusos putant reges ab ecclesia. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: And kings to the brightness of thy rising.

paragraphs.text: {a} Scultet.
As from a watchtower; for so Zion signifieth.
paragraphs.anchor: Lift up thine eyes.

paragraphs.text: See Isa 49:18.
paragraphs.anchor: All they gather themselves together, &c.

paragraphs.text: Like sucking children, they shall suck, and be satisfied. {Isa 66:11} The Vulgate version here hath surgent for sugent; as it hath unus de similibus for unus e millibus {Job 33:23} and evertit for everrit {Luk 15:8} with other such gross mistakes not a few.
paragraphs.anchor: Thy daughters shall be nursed at thy side.

paragraphs.text: Or, Thou shalt break forth as a river; or, Thou shalt shine. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Then thou shalt see and flow together.

paragraphs.text: At first, at least, to see such a confluence of people unto thee.
paragraphs.anchor: And thy heart shall fear.

paragraphs.text: With joy, upon better consideration.
paragraphs.anchor: And be enlarged.

paragraphs.text: i.e., The multitude of the islanders, and such as dwell by the sea side, which are noted for the worst of men, whence the proverb, Maritimi mores. Such are we Britons.
paragraphs.anchor: Because the abundance of the sea

paragraphs.text: {a} ðäø tam de lumine quam de flumine dicitur.
i.e., Of such peoples as usually ride upon camels, viz., the Arabians and the adjacent countries; these shall come flocking and flowing to the Church with their precious and pleasant riches.
paragraphs.anchor: The multitude of camels shall cover thee

paragraphs.text: A lesser and lower kind of camels, commended for their swiftness. {Jer 2:23} We call slow people dromedaries by antiphrasis, and for this, that they can travel four days together without water. Bajazet, beaten by Tamerlane, fled for his life, and might have escaped, had he not stayed to water his mare by the way, which thereupon went the more slowly, and was overtaken by the Tartars.
paragraphs.anchor: The dromedaries.

paragraphs.text: This the ancients interpret as those wise men from the east, {Mat 2:11} which was indeed a small essay of this prophecy. But why should the Papists call them the three kings of Cullen?
paragraphs.anchor: They shall bring gold and incense.

paragraphs.text: This is more than all their rich gifts. A thankful {a} man is worth his weight in the gold of Ophir.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall shew forth the praises of the Lord.

paragraphs.text: {a} Gratanti animo.

i.e., The Kedarenes and Nebateans with their flocks, whereof they had abundance; and they now had hearts to "honour the Lord with their substance, and with the best of their increase." See Isa 23:17-18.
paragraphs.anchor: All the flocks of Kedar

paragraphs.text: Which flieth more swiftly than any bird, and covereth the sky far and near. Deus bone, quam multi catervatim accurrunt! saith the Church here; wonderful! what trooping and treading upon the heels one of another is here! {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Who are these that fly as a cloud?

paragraphs.text: To their columbaries, whereinto they scour and rush gregatim, et mira pernicitate, especially if they have young ones there, or else are driven by some hawk or tempest. {b} God’s people are free hearted; {Psa 110:3} they serve the Lord with cheerfulness. {Psa 100:2} Amor enim alas addit: and well might Plato descant upon the word, Oν θνητοι μεν Eρωτα, Aθανατοι δε περωτα καλουσι, whom men call love, the immortal call winged.
paragraphs.anchor: And as the doves to their windows.

paragraphs.text: {a} Confertis agminibus.
{b} "Columba Radit iter liquidum, celeres neque commovet auras."
They shall come off freely, et non quasi angariati ad auditum verbi et sacramentorum usum. And this is taken to be God’s answer, {a} declaring the cause of that wonderful concourse. {Isa 60:8}
paragraphs.anchor: Surely the isles shall wait for me.

paragraphs.text: i.e., With the first, or, In the beginnings, as the Vulgate hath it. The islands were converted as soon as any, as this of Britain is said to have been by Joseph of Arimathea. Omnium provinciarum prima Britannia publicitus Christi nomen reeepit, saith Sabellicus, {b} Of all proviuces, Britain first embraced the faith of Christ. From the which also, as we first of all the ten kingdoms {Rev 17:7; Rev 17:12} revolted to the Pope, so we were the first that shook off that yoke; our Henry VIII being the first that broke the neck of the Pope’s usurped authority.
paragraphs.anchor: And the ships of Tarshish first

paragraphs.text: By his gracious presence, and the sanctification of his Spirit by the Word.
paragraphs.anchor: Because he hath glorified thee.

paragraphs.text: {a} Huic admirationi Messias ipse respondet.
{b} Ennead. 7, lib. v.
By preaching and writing for the truth, as did many famous Greek and Latin doctors; and since them, not a few of all nations.
paragraphs.anchor: And the sons of strangers shall build up thy walls.

paragraphs.text: As did Cyrus and Darius; but especially Constantine the Great (who cared not what he bestowed upon the Church, and was therefore, in a jeer, by the heathens called Pupillus, as if he needed a guardian to order his expenses), Valentinian, Theodosius, Honorius, Justinian. Our Edward VI, {a} besides the much good he did at home, sent at one time five thousand pounds to relieve Protestants beyond seas. Queen Elizabeth sent both men and means in abundance to the relief of the French and Hollanders.
paragraphs.anchor: And their kings shall minister unto thee.

paragraphs.text: {a} His Life, by Sir John Heywood, p. 115.
Such shall be thy spiritual security, and so great the resort unto thee
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore shall thy gates be open continually.

paragraphs.text: Led captive, saith the Chaldee, sc., to the obedience of faith, {as Psa 149:8} or, Led in state; so others.
paragraphs.anchor: And that their kings may be brought.

paragraphs.text: They are utterly out then, who hold that men may be saved in what religion soever, so be it they lead an honest life. And Pope Julius III is justly accused of sacrilege for stamping money with his own image and this inscription, "The nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish."
paragraphs.anchor: For the nation and kingdom that will not serve thee shall perish.

paragraphs.text: The best cedars there, in allusion to the building of the material temple by Solomon, and afterwards by Ezra; q.d., Whatsoever is good in the world, either in understanding, virtue, or doctrine, shall be sanctified and employed for the building up of the Church.
paragraphs.anchor: The glory of Lebanon.

paragraphs.text: Which from those that would, but cannot, bring better, shall be well accepted.
paragraphs.anchor: The fir tree, the pine tree, and the box tree.

paragraphs.text: ie., My Church, when at lowest, and the members thereof, even the meanest of them. Hence also Christ’s name, "King of kings and Lord of lords," is written "on his thigh," i.e., on his lower parts. {Rev 19:16}
paragraphs.anchor: And I will make the place of my feet glorious

paragraphs.text: When once they shall return and discern between the righteous and the wicked, {as Mal 3:18} there shall be a strange alteration wrought in them, as was in Paul, Cyprian, Vergerius, Latimer, and others.
paragraphs.anchor: The sons also of them that afflicted thee.

paragraphs.text: Such was the custom of the Easterlings; and this, the Popish writers say, is fulfilled in their vicegod, as we may, in the worst sense, best call him. The first that held forth his feet to be kissed was Dioclesian the Tyrant. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Shall bow themselves at the soles of thy feet.

paragraphs.text: {a} Eutrop.

The primitive Christians suffered Odio humani generis, saith Tacitus, {a} through the general hatred conceived against them; and non tam crimen quam nomen puniebatur, saith another, their very name was odious.
paragraphs.anchor: Whereas thou hast been forsaken and hated.

paragraphs.text: Here in part, but hereafter in all perfection. God so favoured the first orthodox Christian emperors, ut cum illorum pietate, Dei liberalitas certare videretur, That God’s liberality might seem to strive with their piety.
paragraphs.anchor: I will make thee an eternal excellency.

paragraphs.text: {a} Lib. xv.
Satiaberis divitiis populorum, saith the Chaldee. Thou shalt be satisfied with the riches of the peoples.
paragraphs.anchor: Thou shalt also suck the milk of the Gentiles.

paragraphs.text: i.e., With kingly dainties and delicacies, saith Zanchez after the Rabbis.
paragraphs.anchor: And shalt suck the breast of kings

paragraphs.text: i.e., I will beautify my Church with far greater gifts of my Spirit than now. The New Jerusalem (which signifieth, say some, the state of the Church in this world), when it shall be refined to the utmost, is all of gold, and these golden times are yet to come.
paragraphs.anchor: For brass I will brlng gold

paragraphs.text: Or, Overseers; thy bishops, say the Septuagint.
paragraphs.anchor: Thine exactors.

paragraphs.text: The full accomplishment of this is not to be expected here.
paragraphs.anchor: Violence shall no more be heard in thy land.

paragraphs.text: sc., When thou hast got the great gulf {Luk 16:26} between thee and thine enemies.
paragraphs.anchor: But thou shalt call thy walls Salvation

paragraphs.text: God will continually come to thee with new benefits, and thou shalt go forth to meet him with thanksgiving. {Psa 89:16}
paragraphs.anchor: And thy gates Praise.

paragraphs.text: God shall be thy sun and shield, thy solace and safety. {Psa 84:11} The light of his loving countenance shall be lifted up upon thee, and this shall be better to thee than all outward comforts.
paragraphs.anchor: The sun shall be no more.

paragraphs.text: Thy joy shall no man take from thee; thou shalt have a habitual cheerfulness.
paragraphs.anchor: Thy sun shall no more go down.

paragraphs.text: Professional saints at least they shall all be, - saints by calling; some of them also shall be really righteous and religious, justified by the merit, and sanctified by the Spirit of Christ. And these together make up a true visible Church, such as was that of Corinth and of Sardis. A mixture there will be to the world’s end.
paragraphs.anchor: Thy people also shall be all righteous.

paragraphs.text: Those that are righteous indeed, are heirs of the world together with faithful Abraham. The meek shall inherit the earth; and as for the poor in spirit, theirs is the kingdom of heaven. {Mat 5:3; Mat 5:5}
paragraphs.anchor: They shall inherit the land for ever.

paragraphs.text: So may some be that yet bear no fruit. {Joh 15:2}
paragraphs.anchor: The branch of my planting.

paragraphs.text: By regeneration. {Eph 2:10} And so are such as are sanctified by habitual infusion, and not by baptismal profession only. In both sorts God is glorified.
paragraphs.anchor: The work of my hands.

paragraphs.text: Three thousand were added to the Church in one day, {Act 2:41} five thousand in another. {Act 4:4} Homo ille tricubitalis, as Chrysostom calleth Paul, that little man, and least of all the apostles, what great pains took he! how many churches planted he! how many thousand souls gained he to Christ! See what a circuit he set, and what a deal of work he despatched at one bout. {Rom 15:18-20} Here was minimus in mille, the least out of a thousand, as it is here. Think the like of the rest of the apostles, as also of Luther, Melanchthon, Ferullus, &c. Mr Foxe telleth us that many were made to see the falsities of Popery by reading Chaucer; more by reading Erasmus’s Colloquies.
paragraphs.anchor: A little one shall become a thousand.

paragraphs.text: Heb., In its time - that is, in the time of the New Testament; but most completely and gloriously at the resurrection shall all these things that are foretold be accomplished.
paragraphs.anchor: I the Lord will hasten it in his time.
